mukta-m0-p20-v476.quick_english: O beloved of my life, please tell me the procedure for the preliminary rites.

mukta-m0-p20-v477.quick_english: O beautiful one, the success of the mantra comes about without effort.

mukta-m0-p20-v478.quick_english: O great goddess, the ramā-seed, the viśva-seed, and the vadhū-seed.

mukta-m0-p20-v479.quick_english: O great goddess, the best practitioner should chant eight thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v480.quick_english: Then the kūrca-seed, the śakti-seed, and after that the kṣa-syllable.

mukta-m0-p20-v481.quick_english: Having become lord of all kingdoms, he indeed wanders upon the earth.

mukta-m0-p20-v482.quick_english: Having recited it with śakti, the wise one should chant nine hundred thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v483.quick_english: Indeed, one should again write the dhūmā-mantra in the middle of the kula-tantra womb.

mukta-m0-p20-v484.quick_english: One obtains victory in battle and destroys enemies in an instant.

mukta-m0-p20-v485.quick_english: Having seen that, the best practitioner should again chant five hundred thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v486.quick_english: Having encased it with the mātṛkā, one should prepare the supreme wealth-giving mantra.

mukta-m0-p20-v487.quick_english: Just as the gods wander, so too does the best practitioner.

mukta-m0-p20-v488.quick_english: Indeed, one should again place the bagalā-mantra in the middle of the eight-petaled diagram.

mukta-m0-p20-v489.quick_english: It indeed brings agitation to the good and crushes enemies in an instant.

mukta-m0-p20-v490.quick_english: It indeed agitates the three worlds; truth, truth, there is no doubt.

mukta-m0-p20-v491.quick_english: Having encased it with the wealth-giver, the wise one should chant ten thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v492.quick_english: The surasundarī great mantra gives complete fruit in the kali age.

mukta-m0-p20-v493.quick_english: The beautiful goddess, in the form of a woman, certainly comes near.

mukta-m0-p20-v494.quick_english: Therefore, O great goddess, it must be done with all effort.

mukta-m0-p20-v495.quick_english: O goddess, one should chant eight thousand times; then one obtains success.

mukta-m0-p20-v496.quick_english: Indeed, a mantra devoid of preliminary rites is thus declared.

mukta-m0-p20-v497.quick_english: Chanting and oblation, libation, consecration, and the feeding of brahmins.

mukta-m0-p20-v498.quick_english: Through great consecration, a person becomes capable in all actions.

mukta-m0-p20-v476.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v476.question: What request does the beloved make regarding the procedure of preliminary rites?
premises: The procedure of preliminary rites is named
A request to tell it is made
mukta-m0-p20-v476.inference: The beloved is asked to explain the procedure of preliminary rites.

mukta-m0-p20-v477.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v477.question: How is success of the mantra attained without effort for the beautiful one?
premises: Success of the mantra is mentioned
mukta-m0-p20-v477.inference: The mantra's success comes effortlessly for the beautiful one.
uncertainties: mastrasya appears as a variant spelling of mantrasya

mukta-m0-p20-v478.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v478.question: Which seed syllables are named in sequence for the great goddess?
mukta-m0-p20-v478.inference: The sequence given is the ramā-seed, viśva-seed, and vadhū-seed.

mukta-m0-p20-v479.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v479.question: How many repetitions must the best practitioner chant for the great goddess?
premises: The best practitioner should chant them
mukta-m0-p20-v479.inference: The best practitioner should chant eight thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v480.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v480.question: Which syllables follow in sequence after the previously named seeds?
mukta-m0-p20-v480.inference: The sequence continues with kūrca-seed, śakti-seed, and then the kṣa-syllable.

mukta-m0-p20-v481.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v481.question: What status does the practitioner attain while wandering on the earth?
premises: One becomes lord of all kingdoms
The wandering occurs on the earth
mukta-m0-p20-v481.inference: Having become lord of all kingdoms, one wanders on the earth.

mukta-m0-p20-v482.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v482.question: What recitation practice must the wise one perform with śakti for nine hundred thousand repetitions?
premises: The wise one is the agent
Nine hundred thousand repetitions should be chanted
mukta-m0-p20-v482.inference: The wise one should recite with śakti and chant nine hundred thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v483.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v483.question: Where must the dhūmā-mantra be written again within the ritual diagram?
premises: The location is the middle of the kula-tantra womb
mukta-m0-p20-v483.inference: The dhūmā-mantra should be written again in the middle of the kula-tantra womb.
uncertainties: kulantrīyonimadhye may reflect a specific diagrammatic term

mukta-m0-p20-v484.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v484.question: What immediate results in battle follow from using this mantra?
premises: The destruction happens in an instant
mukta-m0-p20-v484.inference: One obtains victory in battle and instantly destroys enemies.
uncertainties: vijayamam appears with an unusual final nasal

mukta-m0-p20-v485.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v485.question: What further chanting must the best practitioner perform after seeing that?
premises: The best practitioner has seen that
Five hundred thousand repetitions are specified
The chanting should be done again
mukta-m0-p20-v485.inference: After seeing that, the best practitioner should again chant five hundred thousand times.

mukta-m0-p20-v486.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v486.question: How must the supreme wealth-giving mantra be prepared with the mātṛkā?
premises: It should be made encased by the mātṛkā
mukta-m0-p20-v486.inference: The supreme wealth-giving mantra should be prepared encased by the mātṛkā.

mukta-m0-p20-v487.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v487.question: To whom is the best practitioner compared in manner of wandering?
premises: The gods wander in a certain way
A comparison is drawn with yathā and tathaiva
The best practitioner is the subject
mukta-m0-p20-v487.inference: The best practitioner wanders just as the gods do.

mukta-m0-p20-v488.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v488.question: Where must the bagalā-mantra be placed again within the eight-petaled diagram?
premises: The middle of it is specified
The bagalā-mantra should be placed there again
mukta-m0-p20-v488.inference: The bagalā-mantra should again be placed in the middle of the eight-petaled diagram.
uncertainties: vagalāmantrakaṃ reflects a variant spelling of bagalā

mukta-m0-p20-v489.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v489.question: What dual effects of agitation and crushing does this mantra produce instantly?
premises: Agitation of the good ones is brought about
Both effects occur in an instant
mukta-m0-p20-v489.inference: It agitates the good and instantly crushes enemies.
uncertainties: am is unclear in function here

mukta-m0-p20-v490.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v490.question: What certainty is asserted about the mantra's power to agitate the three worlds?
mukta-m0-p20-v490.inference: It truly agitates the three worlds without any doubt.

mukta-m0-p20-v491.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v491.question: How many repetitions must the wise one chant after encasing with the wealth-giver?
premises: The preparation is encased with the wealth-giver
The wise one is the agent
Ten thousand repetitions should be chanted
mukta-m0-p20-v491.inference: The wise one should encase it with the wealth-giver and chant ten thousand times.
uncertainties: dik sahasraṃ interpreted as ten thousand

mukta-m0-p20-v492.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v492.question: What fruit does the great surasundarī mantra grant in the kali age?
premises: The surasundarī great mantra is named
The context is the kali age
mukta-m0-p20-v492.inference: In the kali age, the surasundarī great mantra grants complete fruit.

mukta-m0-p20-v493.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v493.question: In what form does the beautiful goddess certainly approach the practitioner?
premises: The goddess is beautiful and in woman-form
mukta-m0-p20-v493.inference: The beautiful goddess certainly approaches in the form of a woman.
uncertainties: nikacai and brajati appear as nonstandard spellings

mukta-m0-p20-v494.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v494.question: What obligation follows with all effort for the great goddess?
premises: A conclusion is drawn with therefore
Something must be done for the great goddess
mukta-m0-p20-v494.inference: Therefore it must be done with all effort, O great goddess.

mukta-m0-p20-v495.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v495.question: What result follows from chanting eight thousand times for the goddess?
premises: Eight thousand repetitions should be chanted
mukta-m0-p20-v495.inference: By chanting eight thousand times, one then obtains success.

mukta-m0-p20-v496.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v496.question: How is a mantra declared when it lacks preliminary rites?
premises: A mantra devoid of preliminary rites is mentioned
It is declared in a certain way
The declaration is stated as thus
mukta-m0-p20-v496.inference: A mantra without preliminary rites is thus declared.

mukta-m0-p20-v497.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v497.question: Which ritual acts are listed as components of the preliminary practice?
mukta-m0-p20-v497.inference: The preliminary practice includes chanting, oblation, libation, consecration, and feeding brahmins.
uncertainties: brahmaṇabhojanaṃ may reflect a spelling variant of brāhmaṇabhojanam

mukta-m0-p20-v498.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v498.question: What capability does a person gain in all actions through great consecration?
mukta-m0-p20-v498.inference: Through great consecration, a person becomes capable in all actions.
uncertainties: mahābhiyekāt appears as a variant spelling of mahābhiṣekāt

mukta-m0-p20-v499.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v499.question: What state should a person strive with all effort to attain through consecration?
premises: A conclusion is drawn with therefore
mukta-m0-p20-v499.inference: Therefore a person should strive with all effort to become consecrated.

mukta-m0-p20-v500.speaker: Abhinavagupta (teacher voice)
mukta-m0-p20-v500.question: What duration of observance is prescribed beginning from one ninth lunar day?
premises: The observance begins from a ninth lunar day.
The prescribed period extends until another ninth lunar day.
The optative verb indicates a prescribed duration.
mukta-m0-p20-v500.inference: The observance is to be carried out for a period starting on one ninth lunar day and continuing until the next ninth lunar day.
uncertainties: Whether the period spans consecutive lunar fortnights or a full lunar month is not explicitly specified.

essence: The beloved is asked to explain the procedure of preliminary rites.
The mantra's success comes effortlessly for the beautiful one.
The sequence given is the ramā-seed, viśva-seed, and vadhū-seed.
The best practitioner should chant eight thousand times.
The sequence continues with kūrca-seed, śakti-seed, and then the kṣa-syllable.
